data.title: Tree Composition Calculator
data.statement:
Compute the number of elements at each level of a tree hierarchy.
Each tree is composed of the following levels:
Trees
Trunks
Branches
Small branches
Sticks
Twigs
Leaves
Each level is obtained by multiplying the previous one:
trees = T
trunks = trees × R
branches = trunks × B
small branches = branches × S
sticks = small branches × K
twigs = sticks
A binary [[string]] of length {{7}} is given.
Each character of the string corresponds to one level:

1 means the value of that level is printed
0 means {{0}} is printed instead

The string does not affect the calculations, only the output.
The correspondence is:
Index 0 → trees
Index 1 → trunks
Index 2 → branches
Index 3 → small branches
Index 4 → sticks
Index 5 → twigs
Index 6 → leaves

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

Compute the number of elements at each level of a tree hierarchy.
Each tree is composed of the following levels:
Trees
Trunks
Branches
Small branches
Sticks
Twigs
Leaves
Each level is obtained by multiplying the previous one:
trees = T
trunks = trees × R
branches = trunks × B
small branches = branches × S
sticks = small branches × K
twigs = sticks
A binary string of length 7 is given.
Each character of the string corresponds to one level:

1 means the value of that level is printed
0 means 0 is printed instead

The string does not affect the calculations, only the output.
The correspondence is:
Index 0 → trees
Index 1 → trunks
Index 2 → branches
Index 3 → small branches
Index 4 → sticks
Index 5 → twigs
Index 6 → leaves
Input
Line 1: Seven integers:
T R B S K W L
Line 2: A binary string of length 7.
Output
Line 1: Number of trees.
Line 2: Number of trunks.
Line 3: Number of branches.
Line 4: Number of small branches.
Line 5: Number of sticks.
Line 6: Number of twigs.
Line 7: Number of leaves.
Apply the binary string before printing each value.
Constraints
0 ≤ T ≤ 1000
0 ≤ R ≤ 1000
0 ≤ B ≤ 1000
0 ≤ S ≤ 1000
0 ≤ K ≤ 1000
0 ≤ W ≤ 1000
0 ≤ L ≤ 1000

The binary string has length 7 and contains only 0 and 1.

All test cases are chosen so that every computed value fits in a signed 64-bit integer.
Example
Input
1 1 3 2 2 4 5
1111111
Output
1
1
3
6
12
48
240
